- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5% for 30d horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 7d avg), model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 1–3% from forecast 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.33) within 5 days, model overconfidently holds high prices; reduce forecast mean by 3–7% for next 7d, especially if true outcome shows downward drift.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30d horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply a “lag correction”: subtract 1–4% from first 5 days of forecast if sentiment < 0.75.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is > 10% above 18d history mean, reduce by 2–5% for next 7d unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Sentiment volatility > 0.5 in 3 consecutive days → model overreacts; dampen forecast by 1–3% for next 5d to avoid “noise-driven” peaks.
